subtopics.title: Number Scales on the Country's Road Map

questions.question: On a 1 : 1 500 000 map, one centimetre on paper represents:
The N2 route measures 33 cm on the 1 : 1 500 000 map. The real distance is:
Swellendam is about 225 km from Cape Town by road. On this map that is:
options: 15 cm — ground to paper shrinks, so divide by 15

questions.question: The map answer of 495 km against the signposted 489 km shows that:
options: The map is wrong and should not be used
Scales only work for short distances
Map measurement is honest estimation — a marking guideline allows a small range for ruler accuracy

subtopics.title: Bar Scales and Making a Scale of Your Own

questions.question: A bar scale segment is 3 cm long and labelled 30 km. A pass road measuring 6 cm is:
options: 60 km — each centimetre is worth 10 km

questions.question: After photocopying a map at a reduced size:
options: The bar scale stays true because it shrank with the roads; the printed ratio becomes a lie
The number scale stays true; the bar scale fails

questions.question: A netball court is really 30 m long and its drawing is 12 cm. The scale of the drawing is:
options: 1 : 250 — because 12 : 3 000 in the same units simplifies to 1 : 250

questions.question: A 45 m pool complex must be drawn on a 90 cm display board. The most suitable scale is:
options: 1 : 50, giving a 90 cm plan with no margin
1 : 100, giving a 45 cm plan — as large as the space allows while leaving a margin

questions.question: The index entry 'Ladismith, C4' means the town is found:
options: In the block where column C crosses row 4 — the grid names a block, not a pinpoint
At the corner of the map

questions.question: From Cape Town, Knysna lies to the:
options: East — along the coast to the right of the page

questions.question: Cape Town as seen FROM Knysna lies to the:
options: West — swapping the towns reverses the direction

questions.question: A distance table beats ruler-and-scale for trip planning because:
options: Tables are easier to read than rulers
The ruler cannot measure long roads
The table gives ROAD kilometres, while the ruler takes a straight line your wheels cannot take

subtopics.title: Slope on Maps: Contours and Gradient

questions.question: With a contour interval of 10 m, a trail crossing twelve contour lines has climbed:
options: 120 m — twelve crossings times 10 m each

questions.question: Contours packed close together on a map mean:
options: Steep ground — the height changes quickly over a short distance

questions.question: A trail rises 120 m while covering 1 200 m horizontally. Its gradient is:
options: 1 : 10 — for every 10 m forward, 1 m up

questions.question: Comparing gradients of 1 : 3 and 1 : 10:
options: Neither can be compared without the map
1 : 3 is steeper — the smaller second number packs the same climb into less distance

questions.question: The 'one clever move' before touching the ruler is:
options: Working out what one centimetre is worth — 1 : 1 500 000 means every centimetre is 15 km

questions.question: A map answer of thousands of centimetres for a page distance signals that:
options: You multiplied where you should have divided — the sense test catches it

questions.question: When the map is zoomed on a phone screen, you should trust:
options: The striped bar — it grew along with the roads, so its promise still holds

subtopics.title: Where It Is and Which Way It Lies

questions.question: To find Ladismith from the index entry C4, you:
options: Run down column C, across row 4, and search only that block with your eyes

questions.question: Driving EAST along the N2, the Outeniqua peaks are on your left. Driving home WEST, the same peaks are:
options: On your RIGHT — body directions travel with you; the mountains did not move, you turned around

questions.question: The two 'languages' of direction are:
options: Compass words fixed by the world, and body words — left, right, straight — that travel with the traveller

questions.question: The ruler's straight line between two towns is always:
options: Shorter than the road distance — the table knows the bends

subtopics.title: Reading the Hills Without Climbing Them

questions.question: Each brown contour line on the trail map joins:
options: All ground at the SAME height — walk along it and you stay level
The steepest points of the mountain
The start and end of the trail

questions.question: Two trails cross the same twelve contour lines; one does it in a thumb of map, the other in a full hand. The steeper trail is:
options: The thumb trail — the same climb squeezed into less walking
Neither, since they cross the same lines

questions.question: As ladders against a wall, gradients 1 : 3 and 1 : 10 look like:
options: The 1 : 3 ladder standing nearly upright and the 1 : 10 leaning gently

questions.question: A 7 km trail at a walking pace of 4 km/h takes:
options: 105 minutes — 7 ÷ 4 = 1,75 hours, before water stops and steep sections
